chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Dancing-school gigs and Morton's harmonic knowledge
summary: Butler played dancing schools, and says Morton knew his harmony, was first to put the music on paper, and used simple scales, seventh and ninth chords and occasional diminished.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: So then now I went to dancing school, I'd go into a dancing school and you know, at that time when you're young and them chicks is looking and you're looking too, so we was working --
No. I was only playing -- Morton and I was only playing together. I wasn't -- wasn't anybody playing -- on drums, he had his feet doing that drum work and he always played -- had the bass there.
When you were dealing with him, did you find that he -- how was his harmonic knowledge.
When he played, he knew. (Unintelligible) he was the person who put it on paper. He was the first one to put it on paper.
Now was he using a -- what about -- do you know what -- was he playing any like whole-tone scales.
